req.title: Register form html served
req.statement: The system shall include HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password' in the /auth/register page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-027 requires that GET /auth/register returns an HTTP 2xx response containing HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password'. Three tests are designed: (1) a positive EP test verifying the exact status code 200 and presence of both named input fields in the response body; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that a wrong path (e.g. /auth/register_typo) returns 404, not 200, confirming the route is specifically bound; (3) a boundary BVA test verifying the exact byte-level content of the name attributes to catch mutations that alter the field names (e.g. 'username' -> 'user_name', 'password' -> 'passwd'). Each test is self-contained, uses the in-process Flask test client, and asserts exact values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_register_get_returns_200_with_username_and_password_fields
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary SQLite database
actions: Send GET request to /auth/register using the Flask test client

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_get_returns_200_with_username_and_password_fields():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/register')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'name="username"' in r.data
    assert b'name="password"' in r.data
    os.unlink(path)

test_register_get_returns_200_with_username_and_password_fields()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_get_field_names_are_exactly_username_and_password():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/register')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'name="username"' in r.data
    assert b'name="password"' in r.data
    assert b'name="user_name"' not in r.data
    assert b'name="passwd"' not in r.data
    assert b'name="uname"' not in r.data
    assert b'name="pass"' not in r.data
    os.unlink(path)
